Cook County by the numbers

Who records deeds in Cook County?

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division records, stores and maintains land records for Cook County, including deeds and mortgages. Its office hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m.

Anyone can look up recorded documents on the Clerk's search tool by PIN, grantor, grantee and other indexed details. The Clerk also runs a legal help desk where a volunteer attorney can discuss recording questions, a process to petition to strike unlawful restrictive covenants from old property records, and an e-certify service that verifies electronic certified copies.

  • Search recorded land records by PIN or by party name.
  • Review the Clerk's document requirements before you go.
  • Use the fee schedule to estimate cost, since the final fee is set after the document is inspected.

How much does the Cook County Clerk charge to record a deed?

A deed is priced as Document Class 1 at $107 under the schedule that took effect April 1, 2024. The Clerk says the Office no longer prices documents as standard or non-standard, and nearly every recording now falls into one of seven document classes.

Selected Cook County recording fees. Source: Cook County Clerk, Recording Fees

Any document priced at $107 or more includes a $55 county recording fee, a $23 GIS fee, a $10 document storage fee, an $18 State Rental Housing Support fee and a $1 non-government filer fee. Filers not subject to the state support fee are priced $19 lower.

Why can't the Clerk quote a recording fee by phone?

The final fee can change once staff inspect the document, so the Clerk does not give quotes over the phone. It suggests bringing cash or a credit card, or waiting to fill in the amount on a check until you meet a cashier.

Copies have their own fees: $55 for a paper certified copy, $65 for a certified digital PDF, $27.50 for a non-certified paper copy and $5 for a non-certified download. Copies paid for online carry a 2.10% credit card fee. A DD-214 military discharge, including additional certified copies, is recorded free.

What must a Cook County deed contain to be accepted?

The Clerk's requirements page lists items that every real estate document needs, plus extras for deeds. Missing items are the common reason a recording is turned away.

  • The property must be in Cook County and the document must relate to real estate.
  • Mail-to and prepared-by names and addresses, the common address and the PIN.
  • A legal description, legible type of at least 10 point, and notarization where required.
  • For deeds: grantor and grantee names and addresses, and a completed MyDec for the state and county tax stamps.
  • Municipal real estate transfer tax information, and a grantor and grantee affidavit when the deed is an exempt transaction.

Exempt deeds carry exemption language. The Clerk's example reads "Exempt under Real Estate Transfer Law Tax 35 ILCS 200/31-45 sub par ___ and Cook County Ord. 93-O-27 par ___," followed by a signature and date. Mortgages need the state Anti-Predatory Lending certificate as the first page. Plats must be between 8 1/2 by 14 inches and 30 by 36 inches, submitted as an original with three copies.

How does transfer tax work when a Cook County deed is recorded?

Illinois imposes the transfer tax on transferring title, and the county collects it through revenue stamps sold by the Department of Revenue. If the home stays subject to an existing mortgage, the state says only the owner's equity counts in the tax base, provided the deed or trust agreement says so on its face. The statutes are 35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70.

State law lets a county add a tax of 25 cents per $500 of value, and a home rule municipality may add its own. Because of that layering, the amount due on one Cook County sale depends on the municipality where the house stands. Ask the Clerk or your title company for the stamps and local tax due on your deed.

  • Buyer and seller complete Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, filed in the county where the property sits.
  • Form PTAX-203-A is the supplement for non-residential property sold for more than $1 million.
  • Cook County asks for the MyDec filing before it will accept a deed.

How can a Cook County homeowner guard against deed fraud?

The Clerk's Property Fraud Unit works on forged and fraudulent filings. Its page warns that fraudsters can target homes without a mortgage and file forged documents with the recorder. Once a document is recorded, the owner must petition the court at personal expense to remove it, and selling or refinancing may be impossible until that is resolved.

The Clerk offers a free Property Fraud Alert that calls or emails an owner whenever a document is recorded against the property, including the property of a loved one. Owners who receive an alert can contact the Property Fraud Unit, and staff will research the problem and coordinate with law enforcement where indicated.

What do Census figures show about Cook County homeowners?

Cook County had 2,100,230 households for 2020 to 2024, with 2.43 people per household, according to the Census Bureau. Of residents one year old and over, 88.4% lived in the same house a year earlier. Veterans number 132,321, and 21.7% of residents are foreign born.

The same page reports that 35.8% of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home, and 42.7% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The Treasurer, Assessor and Clerk each handle different pieces of a sale, and the Clerk's piece is the deed.

Which other documents does the Cook County Clerk record around a sale?

A sale often involves more than the deed. The Clerk's requirements page also covers releases of mortgage, assignments, mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices, judgments, contracts, powers of attorney and transfer on death instruments, each with its own checklist.

  • Releases and assignments need the previous recorded document number in addition to the standard items.
  • Powers of attorney and transfer on death instruments need a notarized signature.
  • Judgments need a certified copy, or the original with the judge's original signature.
  • A lis pendens must be signed by the party or an attorney.

If a mortgage payoff is part of your closing, ask the lender or title company when the release will be recorded, and keep the recorded document number for your file. A corrective recording affidavit needs the signatures of every party to the original document.

More questions about Cook County, IL Recorder of Deeds

Where do I record a deed in Cook County?

Record it with the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division. Hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m. Recorded documents can be searched by PIN, grantor or grantee.

What is the recording fee for a Cook County deed?

The posted fee for a deed is $107. Documents not subject to the state rental housing support fee are priced $19 lower. The Clerk cannot give fee quotes by phone.

Can I record a Cook County deed by mail?

Yes. The fee schedule lists recording by mail with return at $5 per document. The deed must still meet the document requirements, including the PIN, legal description and a completed MyDec.

What does a certified copy of a Cook County deed cost?

A paper certified copy is $55 and a certified digital PDF is $65. A non-certified paper copy is $27.50, and a non-certified download is $5. Online card payments add a 2.10% fee.

What is MyDec for Cook County deeds?

MyDec is the state's online system for the transfer declaration and tax stamps. The Clerk's deed requirements list a completed MyDec. The Department of Revenue says buyer and seller complete the PTAX-203 declaration.

Dupage County by the numbers

Who records deeds in DuPage County, Illinois?

The DuPage County Recorder's Office takes in, reviews, records and keeps every deed, mortgage, lien and plat for property in the county. Its collection reaches back to 1839, the year DuPage was cut out of Cook County.

The office is fee funded, so recording charges pay for its operations. Its public line is 630-407-5400 and its research desk answers at 630-407-5401. The counter is open weekdays from 8 a.m. until half past four, and closed on county holidays. Closing companies commonly prepare the deed packet, pay the fees and submit it, so a seller mainly needs to know what gets charged and why.

What fee does the DuPage County Recorder set for a deed?

A standard deed carries an $86.00 filing fee in DuPage County. Nonstandard paper documents cost more, and plats have their own price.

DuPage County Recorder fee schedule for common documents (source: DuPage County Recorder forms and fee schedules)
DocumentRecording fee
Deed (Class 1)$86.00
Lease (Class 2)$86.00

Easement (Class 4)$86.00
Nonstandard document (Class 5)$112.00
Miscellaneous (Class 7)$86.00
Map or plat (Class 8)$110.00
Military discharge (DD214)No charge

The office states that each fee already includes a $10 document storage charge, a $31 geographic information system charge, a $1 real property charge and an $18 Rental Housing Support Program charge. Copies cost $0.50 a page and a certification costs $5.00 a document. Payment comes with the submission, and the office takes credit cards, checks, money orders and cash. Card payments add a convenience fee: $2.00 on charges of $59.99 or less, and 2.75% on $60.00 or more.

What goes into a DuPage County deed package?

You need a completed deed plus the transfer forms that go with it. The Recorder's Office cannot draft a deed or tell you what your particular document must say, so an attorney or title company handles that part.

The office lists these items for a deed package:

  • The signed deed itself
  • The PTAX form or an exemption statement
  • Municipal transfer stamps, where the village or city requires them
  • A metes and bounds affidavit, if one applies
  • The buyer's name and mailing address for the tax bill
  • The property address and the permanent parcel number from the tax bill
  • The legal description
  • The preparer's name and address

A document that is incomplete is returned to whoever sent it. A recorded deed is stamped with a number and date, indexed and imaged, then mailed back to the address given, or returned electronically when it came in through eRecording. To change only the name and mailing address on a tax bill, the office points owners to the County Clerk.

How does transfer tax work on a DuPage County sale?

Illinois charges a state transfer tax through revenue stamps sold at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. The Recorder sells the stamps, and since paper stamps were phased out at the end of 2025, counties issue electronic stamps or similar proof of payment.

Each sale also needs a signed real estate transfer declaration, Form PTAX-203, with at least one seller and one buyer (or their agents) signing. The Illinois Department of Revenue handles questions about the form and the MyDec online tool at 844-445-1114. The DuPage Recorder has accepted MyDec-prepared forms since January 14, 2015.

Some deeds are exempt from the tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-45. The DuPage list includes deeds where the actual consideration is under $100, tax deeds, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier recorded deed, deeds of partition, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. Deeds exempt under paragraphs (b), (k) or (m) of the county list still need a PTAX-203. The county references its own Resolution F11879 for local transfer rules, so ask the Recorder which stamps your deed needs.

Which DuPage municipalities charge their own transfer stamp?

Some do, and some do not. The Recorder publishes a list of municipal fees and tells owners to contact the village or city before closing, since the amounts can change without notice to the office.

  • Elmhurst: $1.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $30.00
  • Addison: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00
  • Wheaton: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Woodridge: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Naperville: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Glen Ellyn: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Carol Stream: $3.00 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Bolingbrook: $7.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00

The county page also lists Aurora, Bartlett, Elk Grove, Glendale Heights and Hanover Park. For a town missing from that list, ask the village or city hall whether a local stamp applies before closing.

Can I record a deed online in DuPage County?

Yes. The Recorder accepts deeds, mortgages, releases, liens and similar documents through electronic recording. Plats and DD-214 discharge forms are not accepted electronically.

Electronic recording runs through an account with an approved vendor. The county names Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Any setup fee is a matter between the customer and the vendor. Most sellers never open such an account, because their closing company already has one.

The other routes are to hand the document in at the office or mail it to the office's mailing address. Documents recorded electronically come back electronically.

How far back do DuPage County property records go?

The office keeps records from 1839 to the present. Computer searches cover names from 1961, parcel numbers from 1985 and property addresses from 1995, and plats can be searched back to the 1800s.

Searching and printing images through the online search is free. A copy of a deed shows who owns the property but says nothing about liens, so it is not a substitute for a title search. The office states that it does not run full title searches and carries no errors and omissions coverage, so a title insurance company does that work. A copy of a satisfaction shows that a mortgage was paid off once it has been recorded.

What is DuPage County like for a home seller?

DuPage County sits west of Chicago and is one of the collar counties of the metro area. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 934,298 residents, and the county seat is Wheaton, with Naperville as the largest city. It touches Cook County to the east and north, Will County to the south, Kane County to the west and Kendall County at a corner.

QuickFacts reports 370,517 housing units, a 73.1% owner-occupied rate and a median value of $391,400 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 through 2024. Median household income for the same period is $112,096 and median gross rent is $1,688. The county covers 327.80 square miles of land and drew 1,265 building permits in 2025.

Employers include Oak Brook's Hub Group and Ace Hardware, Naperville's Nicor Gas, Lisle's Molex and the two national laboratories, Argonne in the southeast and Fermilab on the Kane County line. Oakbrook Center, Fox Valley Mall and Yorktown Center anchor the shopping.

How are property taxes handled around a DuPage County closing?

Property tax is billed in arrears, so a bill issued in 2026 covers the 2025 tax year. DuPage mails one bill with two payment coupons, and for 2025 taxes the installments were due June 1 and September 1, 2026, both of which have passed.

The Treasurer's Office, at 630-407-5900, collects the tax but does not set values, so questions about an assessment go to the assessor whose number is on the bill. The County Clerk calculates the tax on each parcel and certifies it to the Treasurer. Look for the exemptions listed on the bill, since the Treasurer reports that both the general homestead and senior exemptions are $8,000 each. If a mortgage company pays the bill, a yellow box on the bill says so, and a second payment would only create a refund request. The Treasurer reports just under $4 million in such duplicate payments in a recent year.

More questions about DuPage County, IL Recorder of Deeds

What is the DuPage County deed filing price?

The DuPage County Recorder charges $86.00 for a standard deed. That price includes storage, GIS, real property and rental housing support charges. A nonstandard document costs $112.00 and a plat $110.00. Card payments carry a convenience fee on top.

Does the DuPage County Recorder write or review my deed?

No. The office checks that a document meets recording requirements but cannot prepare a deed or give legal advice. Deed forms come from an attorney, a title company or a form seller, and an incomplete package is returned to the sender.

Do I pay Illinois transfer tax if I sell my DuPage County house?

Usually yes, because the state tax is collected through revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 of value when the deed is recorded. Certain deeds are exempt under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, such as tax deeds and corrective deeds. Exempt deeds in some categories still need a PTAX-203.

Can I look up my deed online for free in DuPage County?

Yes. The Recorder's online search lets you view and print document images at no charge. A deed copy proves ownership but shows nothing about liens, so use a title search for that. In person or by mail, copies cost $0.50 a page.

Where do I send questions about my DuPage County tax bill?

Call the DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 for payments and the County Clerk at 630-407-5500 for tax calculation questions. Questions about the assessed value go to the township assessor listed on the bill. The Recorder's Office does not handle assessments.

Lake County by the numbers

Who records deeds in Lake County, Illinois?

Lake County has no stand-alone recorder. Deeds are recorded by the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office, on the 6th floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Deeds are accepted in person or by mail.

The division's phone is 847-377-2575 and its fax is 847-984-5860. Once a deed is recorded, it gets a document number, is scanned and entered in a grantor and grantee index, and the original goes back to the party named on the document. The division's calendar lists closures for holidays such as Veterans Day and Thanksgiving, so a closing that depends on same-day recording is worth confirming with the office. The county's own pamphlet adds a reminder that the staff do not replace legal and accounting advice about the effect of a deed change.

What does Lake County charge to record a deed?

A deed is a standard document in Lake County, and a standard document costs $70. The Clerk's schedule says the only extra charges collected at recording are the state and county real estate transfer taxes that come due on a sale.

Lake County Clerk recording fees by document type (source: Lake County Clerk, Recording and Copy Fees)
DocumentFee
Standard document, including most deeds$70
Standard document from a government agency exempt from the rental housing surcharge$50
Non-standard document$82
Non-standard document from an exempt government agency$62
Federal or state lien, lien release, UCC termination$43
UCC-1 and UCC-3 filings$58

Copies of recorded documents are $1 per page, plats are $5 per page, and a PTAX form is $1. Military discharges are free to the veteran. The office takes cash, checks made out to the Lake County Clerk, and Discover, MasterCard or Visa.

Which Lake County documents count as non-standard?

The Clerk applies the definition in 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1, and anything outside it is treated as standard. The schedule lists six situations that push a document into the higher fee:

  • It divides an active tax parcel number into new parcels
  • It is recorded under the Uniform Commercial Code
  • It does not meet the paper and layout rules, such as 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, black ink, white 20-pound paper, half-inch margins and a blank 3 by 5 inch space at the upper right of page one
  • It is a state or federal lien
  • It refers to more than 5 tax parcel numbers in the county
  • It refers to more than 5 other recorded document numbers

A deed that is printed cleanly on letter paper with no staples on attachments and no more than five parcel numbers stays at the $70 level.

What must a Lake County deed include?

The county's recording pamphlet lists ten requirements, and a deed missing one is likely to be turned back. In short:

  • It is dated, signed and notarized
  • The parties are named, with the buyer's address
  • It carries a full legal description, plus a Plat Act affidavit if the description uses metes and bounds
  • It shows the preparer's name and address
  • It gives a mail-to name and address for the return of the recorded deed
  • It lists the taxpayer name and address for future tax bills
  • It comes with a completed PTAX-203 or a signed and dated exemption statement
  • It has any municipal transfer stamps obtained beforehand

Titles to mobile homes are not recorded here. In Illinois those are registered with the Secretary of State, which has offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.

How is transfer tax collected on a Lake County sale?

Lake County collects two transfer taxes at recording. The county pamphlet states the state rate as 50 cents per $500 and the county rate as 25 cents per $500, figured on the PTAX-203. The state rate matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15, which also required counties to move from paper stamps to electronic stamps or similar proof of payment by December 31, 2025.

The state's MyDec website prepares the PTAX-203 online. A transfer that qualifies for an exemption instead carries a signed, dated exemption statement on the deed.

Local stamps are a different matter. Deeds for property in or mailing to Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa or North Chicago require a stamp or a signed exemption certificate from that municipality before the deed goes to the Clerk. Contact the municipal office first, since the Clerk will not obtain it for you.

Can a Lake County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. Most deeds are eligible for eRecording through the Clerk's Speed eRecord service, and authorized business submitters prepare packages through CSC, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox or Simplifile. Staff review each package and either approve it or send it back with the reason, and a clean package can be recorded within minutes.

Two limits apply. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot go through the system, so a revenue deed needs a MyDec declaration. And deeds for the six municipalities above need the stamp or exemption certificate before submission. The standard recording fees apply, and the vendors add their own processing fee.

Individual homeowners generally go through a title company or attorney rather than opening an account themselves.

How should the deed state the form of ownership?

The county's pamphlet defines the common forms. Sole ownership leaves no other person with an interest. Joint tenancy gives two or more people equal undivided interests, and when one dies the share passes to the surviving joint tenants rather than to heirs. Tenancy by the entirety is a form for spouses that passes the whole property to the survivor without probate. Tenancy in common allows unequal shares and carries no right of survivorship.

Which form fits belongs to the attorney who prepares the deed. A sale deed usually names the seller as grantor in whichever form title is currently held.

What should a seller know about Lake County itself?

Lake County sits in the northeast corner of Illinois on Lake Michigan, with Waukegan as seat and largest city. It covers 1,368 square miles in total but only 444 of those are land, making it the second-largest Illinois county by total area and the only one with more water than land.

The Census Bureau counted 714,342 residents in 2020 and estimates 719,339 in July 2025. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a 74.8% owner-occupied rate, a median home value of $345,700 and median household income of $110,416. The county has 18 townships and dozens of villages and cities, including Highland Park, Lake Forest, Gurnee, Libertyville, Mundelein and Vernon Hills. Interstates 94 and 41 and U.S. 12, 14 and 45 cross it.

School districts matter to many sellers here. High school districts include Adlai E. Stevenson 125, Libertyville 128, Lake Forest 115, Warren Township 121 and Zion-Benton 126, among others.

More questions about Lake County, IL Recorder of Deeds

Is there a Recorder of Deeds office in Lake County, Illinois?

Yes, but it is run as the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office at 18 N County Street, 6th floor, in Waukegan. The phone is 847-377-2575.

How much is the recording fee for a deed in Lake County?

The fee is $70 for a standard document, which covers most deeds. A non-standard document costs $82, and the only other charges at recording are the transfer taxes due on a sale.

How much is Lake County's transfer tax?

The county pamphlet gives the state rate as 50 cents per $500 and the county rate as 25 cents per $500. Six municipalities, including Highland Park and Lake Forest, also require their own stamp or exemption before recording.

Can I record a deed with a paper PTAX-203 through eRecording?

No. The Clerk states that deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted through eRecording, so an electronic revenue deed needs a MyDec declaration instead.

Where are mobile home titles recorded in Lake County?

They are not recorded with the Clerk. Illinois registers mobile home titles through the Secretary of State, with offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.

What role does the Will County Recorder of Deeds play in a home sale?

After a sale, the Recorder of Deeds is the office that places the new deed on the public record. You will find it at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, and the number is (815) 740-4637. Its published price list spans standard documents, uniform commercial code filings, plats, state and federal paperwork and certified copies, so a deed is one of several filings handled there.

With 696,355 residents at the 2020 census, Will County ranks fourth in Illinois. Joliet is the seat, Naperville, Bolingbrook and Plainfield sit within its lines, and a deed for any parcel in the county is filed at this single office.

The recorder's site also points customers to Fidlar products such as Official Records Online, Laredo and Tapestry, which are the platforms used for searching and submitting records.

What are the recording fees in Will County?

Recording a standard document costs $90.00. The county board approved Resolution 25-224 on August 21, 2025, under Public Act 103-0884, and the new schedule started October 1, 2025. Anything the office receives from that day forward is charged under it.

Fee schedule in force since October 1, 2025, from the Will County Recorder

Non-standard document$118.00

These charges sit apart from the transfer tax and from whatever the title company bills for preparing and submitting the deed.

What qualifies a document for the standard fee?

The office applies the standard fee to a document that satisfies the paper and layout rules in state law and keeps its references to a limited number.

  • Loose sheets sized 8.5 by 11 inches, neither permanently bound nor on a continuous form.
  • Legible black ink, whether typed, printed or handwritten, though signatures and dates may be in another color if they copy clearly.
  • White paper weighing 20 pounds or more, with half-inch clean margins on all four sides.
  • An empty 3 by 5 inch block in the upper right corner of page one.
  • Nothing stapled or otherwise attached to a page.
  • No more than five Property Identification Numbers and five related document numbers.

Graphics that accompany a document can be as large as 11 by 17 inches at no added cost. A document that misses these standards is recorded only once the extra fee is paid.

What pushes a deed into the non-standard class?

Anything that fails the standard test is charged $118.00. The schedule names three triggers.

  • A legal-size (8.5 by 14) page, unless it is an exhibit drawing or plat.
  • Six or more Property Identification Number references.
  • Six or more related document number references.

A plat filed alone is also non-standard. It must measure at least 11 by 17 inches and no more than 30 by 36, a range that takes in miscellaneous plats, easements and dedications.

A deed for a house on one parcel normally qualifies as standard when it is printed correctly. The higher fee tends to show up when a deed bundles several lots or cites a long list of earlier documents, so have the title agent count the parcel numbers before filing.

What is the RHSP surcharge?

The $90.00 and $118.00 rates carry a $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge. The schedule drops that surcharge for documents recorded by federal, state or local government agencies, and the result is the $71.00 and $99.00 exempt rates.

A deed from a private seller is not a government filing, so the full rate applies. The exempt rows serve agencies, and state and federal documents are listed at $71.00. If it is unclear whether a filer counts as a government body, ask the office first so the check carries the right amount.

How is the Illinois transfer tax charged on a Will County sale?

The state taxes the privilege of transferring title at 50 cents for every $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the unpaid mortgage balance is left out of the base.

It is due even if no document is ever recorded, and it reaches related transactions as a group. The recorder collects it through revenue stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-15). Paper stamps were to be retired by December 31, 2025, with counties then issuing electronic stamps or similar indicia, and every sale recorded is reported to the Department of Revenue electronically.

Your contract decides who pays, and the settlement statement shows the line. Ask the Recorder and your municipality whether a local transfer tax applies in addition.

Which Will County deeds escape the transfer tax?

Section 31-45 keeps a short, specific list of exemptions, and several entries touch homeowners and heirs.

  • Deeds with actual consideration under $100.
  • Deeds that confirm, correct, modify or supplement an earlier recorded deed for no added consideration.
  • Tax deeds.
  • Deeds releasing property that secured a debt.
  • Deeds of partition.
  • Deeds given to a mortgage holder through foreclosure or a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.

The declaration is still required for some exempt deeds, such as certain governmental, charitable and exchange deeds, so an exemption does not always excuse the form.

What Will County market facts shape a deed filing?

Volume is the main story. The Census Bureau counts 259,218 housing units in Will County as of 2025, with owners in 82.8% of occupied homes and a midpoint home value of $319,600 for 2020 to 2024. Builders pulled 1,993 permits in 2025, so new-construction deeds, plats and subdivision filings arrive alongside resales.

That mix explains the fee table. Subdivision and condominium plats cost $144.00 each, and a developer's filing with many parcel numbers lands in the non-standard class, while a plain resale deed for one lot is the cheap case. Residents of Joliet, Naperville, Bolingbrook, Plainfield, Romeoville and the villages in between all record at the same counter in Joliet.

The recorder's website names Fidlar's Official Records Online, Laredo and Tapestry among its systems. Ask your title company which channel it uses to submit the deed.

How does a deed get recorded in Will County?

Title companies usually prepare the deed and send it in, so sellers rarely visit the counter. A family transfer without a title company calls for these steps.

  1. Check the layout, including the 3 by 5 inch empty block on page one.
  2. List each Property Identification Number, keeping to five or fewer for the standard fee.
  3. Fill out the transfer declaration and settle the transfer tax with the office.
  4. Pay the fee and tax, then keep the stamped copy or confirmation.
  5. Order a certified copy at $42.00 if a lender or court wants one.

Before filing, settle property tax with the county Treasurer. Unpaid installments stay with the parcel and accrue interest under state law, so a payoff letter protects both buyer and seller.

More questions about Will County, IL Recorder of Deeds

What does Will County charge to file a deed?

Standard documents cost $90.00 and non-standard ones $118.00 under the October 1, 2025 schedule, with exempt rates of $71.00 and $99.00.

Where do I find the Will County Recorder?

At 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, phone (815) 740-4637, website willcountyrecorder.com.

How is the transfer tax figured?

Fifty cents for each $500 of declared value or fraction of $500. A mortgage the property passes subject to is left out of the base.

Does a quitclaim deed avoid the transfer tax?

Not automatically. The exemption list covers deeds with consideration under $100, correction deeds and certain others, and a deed with a higher stated value follows the normal rule.

What does a certified copy cost?

$42.00 under the October 2025 schedule. Call before ordering, because the county board can change fees by resolution.

The office lists fewer rejections, quicker corrections and savings on postage among the benefits, so check with your title company or settlement lawyer whether they send documents electronically.

How much is the Illinois transfer tax on a Champaign County sale?

The state levies a tax on the privilege of transferring title, of fifty cents on every $500 of value, rounded up for any fraction, as stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). When the transferring document says the property is transferred subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis. The tax is due whether or not a document is recorded.

The recorder collects it through revenue stamps. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, and counties issue electronic stamps or alternative indicia afterward, reporting through MyDec. Ask the Clerk and Recorder or your title company which local charges, if any, appear on your settlement statement.

Section 31-45 lists deeds exempt from the tax. These are some of them:

  • Deeds to or from a governmental body, or from certain charitable, religious or educational organizations.
  • Deeds that secure a debt, and deeds that release property held as security.
  • Deeds that only confirm, correct or supplement a deed already recorded.
  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Tax deeds, deeds of partition, and deeds given to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.

Some exempt deeds still need the declaration filed, so check the statute text before skipping the form.

What does Champaign County look like for people recording a sale?

Champaign County had an estimated 209,972 residents by mid-2025, across about 996 square miles, and the Census Bureau shows 54.0% of housing units owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024. The middle owner-occupied home was worth $211,500, and rent at the midpoint was $1,051 a month. Urbana is the seat, Champaign is the biggest city, and the University of Illinois sits between them.

The Clerk and Recorder works from the county's Urbana offices, while a separate office, the Treasurer, collects the tax on those same parcels. A student rental in Champaign, a ranch house in Mahomet and a farm parcel near a village will each record the same way, but their prior-owner tax bills and any unpaid installments can differ widely. Pull the PIN history from the Treasurer before the deed goes in.

What follows once the deed reaches the land records?

Recording moves the property into the new owner's name in the land records, and the tax side follows separately. The Champaign County Treasurer tells new owners to check their closing documents, title company or attorney to see whether tax is owed. If the bill went to the previous owner, that person has to forward it, and the Treasurer will send a duplicate on request at 217-384-3743.

A seller who wants a clean exit should confirm that both installments for the year are paid or credited on the settlement statement. Unpaid taxes become part of the annual sale in late October, and redemption after a sale runs through the County Clerk, so a missed payment turns into a second office visit later.

What else does the recorder's office handle?

Beyond deeds, the office accepts veterans' DD-214 discharge papers at no charge. A veteran brings the original, the staff scan it, create a permanent record and return the original. A certified copy later requires a government-issued ID, and military discharge papers less than 62 years old are not available to the public.

State and federal tax liens and releases are recorded for $51 each. Releases of a mortgage you paid off are recorded here too, and a release needs the document number of the mortgage it satisfies. Before listing a house, have your title company search for open mortgages and liens so a release can be recorded ahead of closing.

More questions about Champaign County, IL Recorder of Deeds

What does filing a deed run in Champaign County?

$70 for a standard real estate document, or $82 if it misses one of the office's requirements. The office has announced a $10 increase effective December 1, 2026.

Is a MyDec declaration required before a Champaign County deed is accepted?

Yes. Every deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption, and the county runs all property transactions through MyDec.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Champaign County?

Yes. Approved partners such as Simplifile, ePN and CSC eRecording submit documents over the internet, and they are recorded and returned the same day.

What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?

Fifty cents on each $500 of declared value, with any fraction counted as a full unit, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Mortgage balances left in place are excluded from the basis.

When is the recorder's office open?

Weekdays from 8 until 4:30, except major holidays, with a 9 o'clock start on the second Wednesday of each month.

Where do you file a deed in Lee County, Illinois?

File it with the Lee County Clerk and Recorder, whose desk is up one flight in the Old Lee County Courthouse, 112 E Second Street, Dixon. The same staff issues birth, death and marriage records, registers assumed names, runs elections, and deals with delinquent taxes. Call 815-288-3309, or write to P.O. Box 329, Dixon, IL 61021. The counter is open Monday to Friday from 8 until half past four, except legal holidays.

Lee County spreads over about 725 square miles of northern Illinois farmland and river towns, and Dixon is its seat. The county was cut from the southern half of Ogle County in 1839, and its boundaries have held steady since. Neighbors are Ogle, DeKalb, LaSalle, Bureau and Whiteside. The Census Bureau counts 15,027 housing units for July 1, 2025, and 90.5% of residents had not moved in the prior year. Owners stay put, so many deeds here arrive through inheritance, trusts or estate transfers, and those files need extra care.

Bring the vesting deed with you. The recorder's staff cannot supply a legal description, so it has to be copied word for word from a prior deed or a title report.

What are the Lee County recording charges?

Plan on $88 for an ordinary instrument such as a warranty deed, quitclaim deed or mortgage release. A document exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee costs $69. The county's predictable fee schedule is dated July 1, 2023 and cites 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1. An Illinois act signed in February 2023 added $9 to the Rental Housing Support fee, effective that same July 1.

Payment is by cash or check, and the counter takes no debit or credit cards. Enclose a stamped envelope addressed to yourself, and hand over an original or certified copy only. Copies of a veteran's discharge cost nothing. Transfer tax is a separate charge, covered below.

What page layout will the Lee County recorder accept?

An instrument that meets the county's layout rules pays the lower charge, and one that misses them costs $97. The Recording page sets out these requirements:

  • Separate 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, unbound and not on a continuous form, with any attached graphic no larger than 11 by 17 inches.
  • Black ink that is easy to read, whether written by hand, typed or printed. Dates and signatures may be in another color if they copy cleanly.
  • White stock of 20-pound weight or heavier, leaving a half inch of blank margin all around.
  • An empty 3 by 5 inch box in the top right corner of page one.
  • Nothing stapled or taped onto a page, though sheets can be stapled to each other.

Recorder staff do not provide legal opinions, legal descriptions or title searches, whether you ask at the counter or by telephone. Copy the description from your vesting deed or ask the title company, and have an attorney draft any document that moves ownership.

Is a Plat Act affidavit part of a Lee County deed?

Nearly always. The county wants a plat act affidavit, or a stated exemption, with every deed. The one carve-out is a deed within the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. Its posted form states that the transfer is exempt from the Illinois Plat Act (765 ILCS 205) and offers boxes for reasons, such as the conveyance not dividing a parcel.

A missing affidavit is a frequent cause of a returned deed. Anyone selling off part of a lot or a field should talk to the assessment office and a surveyor before drafting, because splitting land is exactly where the exemption stops working.

What does Illinois charge to transfer title, and what must be signed?

Illinois sets its tax on transferring title at a half dollar for each $500 slice of value, with a partial slice counting as a full one, using the figure on the declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). A deed that says the property passes subject to a mortgage leaves the outstanding loan balance out of the math. Counties collect through revenue stamps, and the statute set December 31, 2025 as the date to replace paper stamps with electronic ones or similar marks (35 ILCS 200/31-15).

The declaration needs a signature from at least one seller and at least one buyer, or from attorneys or agents for them. It must reach the recorder with the deed, or within 3 business days of the transfer if that is sooner (35 ILCS 200/31-25). Expect questions on price, parcel number, legal description, deed type, address, improvements, homestead exemptions shown on the last bill, and whether the parties are related or the sale was compulsory.

A few deeds owe no tax, among them tax deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and deeds delivered to a lender through foreclosure or in lieu of it (35 ILCS 200/31-45). Several of those must still carry a declaration. Ask the Clerk and Recorder whether anything local sits on top of the state charge.

What becomes of the transfer declaration after recording?

The recorder does not file the declaration with the deed. Staff write the deed's document number on the declaration and forward it to the chief county assessment officer within 30 days. That office adds the assessed value and sends it on to the Illinois Department of Revenue (35 ILCS 200/31-30). It is how the assessment staff learn that a Lee County parcel sold, and for how much.

So an accurate form protects both sides. It also bears on the seller's homestead exemption: the statute leaves the credit in place through the assessment year of the sale, and the assessment office may ask the next owner to apply for the following year (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

Does Lee County take electronic recordings?

Yes, from approved submitters only, between 8:30 in the morning and 3:30 in the afternoon. The county names four partners:

  • Corporation Service Company, at erecording.com
  • eRecording Partners Network, at goepn.com
  • Simplifile, at simplifile.com
  • Hopdox, at hopdox.com

Title companies and closing attorneys usually use one of these on the day of closing. For a family transfer with no title company involved, send the paper original with a check and a stamped return envelope, or bring it to the counter.

What should a Lee County seller verify before the deed goes in?

Start by searching the parcel on the county's property tax inquiry site to confirm who is the owner of record. Then call the Treasurer at 815-288-4477 to learn whether any year is unpaid or sold. A buyer's title search surfaces open mortgages, liens and judgments, and each must be released of record or paid off at closing.

Inherited property takes extra steps. The grantor on the deed must be whoever actually holds title, and that can mean a personal representative with court papers. Repairs, tenants or back taxes do not change how recording works. They change who pays what at the closing table.

More questions about Lee County, IL Recorder of Deeds

What is the Lee County charge for an ordinary deed?

$88, or $69 if the document is exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, under the schedule dated July 1, 2023. A document that names six or more parcel numbers, or misses the layout rules, costs $97.

Will the Lee County recorder accept a credit card?

No. The Recording page says the counter takes cash or check only. Electronic filers go through one of four approved e-recording partners instead.

How is the Illinois transfer tax figured?

A half dollar for each $500 of value, with a partial $500 counted as a whole, per 35 ILCS 200/31-10. The balance of a mortgage the buyer takes over is left out when the deed says the transfer is subject to it.

Does every Lee County deed need a plat affidavit?

Every deed except those in the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. The county requires the affidavit or a stated exemption, and its website posts the form.

When can a title company e-record in Lee County?

Between 8:30 in the morning and 3:30 in the afternoon. Only approved submitters qualify, and the county currently lists Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hopdox.

Madison County by the numbers

What does the Madison County Recorder do?

The Madison County Recorder records, indexes and keeps every document that transfers land in the county. The land record begins in 1812, the year the county was created, and it establishes who owns what. Besides deeds, mortgages, liens, trusts and easements, the office records military discharge papers (DD-214) and out-of-county birth certificates and marriage licenses.

The office is at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025, the same building that houses the Treasurer and the Board of Review. The counter opens at half past eight on weekdays and closes at half past four, with holiday closures. The phone is 618-296-4475 and the email is recorder@madisoncountyil.gov.

For a seller, the Recorder is where the sale becomes public record. Recording here puts the sale on the public record. Your title company or closing attorney normally handles the filing, but you should know what the office will look for.

What does a Madison County deed need before it is recorded?

A deed has to meet several state and county requirements, and the Recorder's office will not accept one that misses them. The office's documents page lists these:

  • A completed Illinois Department of Revenue Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a Statement of Exemption.
  • The name and address of the grantee for tax billing purposes, required by 55 ILCS 5/3-5020. Madison County counts as a county of the second class, with a population over 25,000 and not over 1,000,000.
  • A Plat Act Affidavit with every deed, with the form and instructions posted on the county website.
  • A permanent parcel number. A county board resolution requires one on all deeds and documents that transfer property.
  • The name and address of the person to whom the document should be returned.
  • The name and address of whoever prepared the instrument, printed or stamped on its face (55 ILCS 5/3-5022). Court orders, wills, death certificates and instruments signed outside Illinois are excluded.

A release must also give the recorder's document number of the mortgage it releases, or the book and page where applicable. A document number is preferred. If the deed carries money, the office wants the recording fee and the transfer tax paid separately when you pay by check.

What transfer tax applies in Madison County?

Two layers of tax apply to the declared price, and both are stated per $500 or part of $500 of taxable consideration. The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500, and the County of Madison collects $.25 per $500. The county's page lists the full set of exemptions in the office, on the website and in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

Madison County transfer tax rates as printed on the Recorder's documents page

County of Madison$.25 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration

The PTAX declaration asks you to work out the net taxable consideration. The Department of Revenue supplies the forms, and the Recorder cannot take a deed and declaration until all required information is filled in. For questions on the form, call the Recorder, or reach the state revenue agency's Springfield line at 217-782-4568.

Recording fees are set separately. Ask the Recorder's office for the current fee schedule before you mail or send a payment, because the amount depends on the document type.

Which documents does the Madison County Recorder accept?

The office records a long list of instruments, and deeds, mortgages and releases make up most of the volume. The types named on its list include warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, trustee's, executor's, administrator's, guardian's, conservator's, sheriff's and tax deeds, deeds in trust, easements, leases, contracts for deed, mortgage assignments and modifications, mechanic's liens, lis pendens, state and federal tax liens, plats and plats of survey, UCC filings and notices of probate.

A few categories carry their own rules:

  • Plats require the original plat and two copies, one mylar and one paper, plus a surveyor's certificate, a legal description, a school district statement and a 9-1-1 coordinator's certificate.
  • State tax liens trace to Chapter 35 ILCS, Act 5, Article 11, and federal tax liens come through the Internal Revenue Service.
  • A memorandum of judgment must show the court, date, amount, case number, the winning party and the last known address of the losing party.
  • Contracts for deed and sales contracts follow 765 ILCS 86/10-5.

Mortgage releases follow 765 ILCS 905/2. For a seller with an old mortgage, confirm that the lender's release was recorded, because an unrecorded release can stall a closing.

How do you get copies from the Madison County Recorder?

Send copy requests to recordercopies@madisoncountyil.gov with the reference number of the document. The office does not do title searches, so the reference number is what lets staff locate it. Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, and turnaround is 5 to 7 business days, though staff try to move faster.

To find a number yourself, use the parcel number on your tax bill. The county's parcel format breaks down by township, land or lot, map, block and parcel. In the sample 14-2-15-10-20-303-007.001, the first 14 is the old township number, the 2 means a subdivided lot, and the 007 is the parcel with an 001 split suffix. Ending codes show the class: R00 for residential or farm, C00 commercial, A00 agricultural lease and D00 for TIF and enterprise zone parcels.

What does a Madison County seller do about taxes at the Recorder's office?

Most of the tax work happens before the deed reaches the Recorder. Confirm the installments are paid with the Treasurer, which bills in July, September, October and December, so a closing in between can leave a partly paid year. Make sure the grantee's tax bill address is on the deed. The Recorder will not record a deed without it, and a wrong address sends the next bill to the wrong place.

The county has a land record going back more than two centuries, and the title search behind your sale draws on it. If you are selling a house with problems, such as an unreleased old mortgage or a probate gap, have the title company check the Recorder's index early so those items are fixed before the closing date.

How does a Madison County deed fit into a house sale?

A typical sale in Madison County moves in a set order. The title company orders a search against the Recorder's index, the seller signs a deed, the parties complete the PTAX declaration or claim an exemption, and the closer submits everything for recording. The transfer tax is computed from the declared consideration, and the state and county shares are collected together when the deed is accepted.

Because the office will not take a deed missing its required items, errors cost days. The most common fixes come from the list above: a missing parcel number, no return address, no preparer statement, or a Plat Act Affidavit left out of the package. A seller who hands the closer a tax bill with the full parcel number and the buyer's mailing address avoids most of these.

If your property sits inside a subdivision, ask whether a plat covers it, since plats have their own recording rules and may be needed to answer title questions. If you hold the property in a trust, say so at the start, because deeds in trust and trustee's deeds are separate document types on the Recorder's list. Sellers who inherited a home should bring the probate paperwork, since a notice of probate and an executor's or administrator's deed are also recorded documents in this office.

More questions about Madison County, IL Recorder of Deeds

Where is the Madison County Recorder's office?

It is at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025. Weekday hours run from half past eight in the morning to half past four in the afternoon, with holiday closures.

The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration, and Madison County collects $.25 per $500 or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or exemption statement goes with the deed.

Yes. A county board resolution requires a permanent parcel number on all deeds and documents affecting transfers of property. Use the number printed on your tax bill.

How much does a copy of a recorded document cost?

Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a 5 to 7 business day turnaround. Include the reference number, since the office does not do title searches.

Does the deed need the buyer's address?

Yes. Illinois law requires the grantee's name and address for tax billing purposes on any conveyance recorded in a county of the first or second class, and Madison County is a second class county.

Can a Peoria County deed be recorded electronically?

Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, accompanies every deed. Peoria County joined the state's MyDec system, which lets the declaration be submitted online before recording. In the state's description, buyer and seller prepare the form together and file it with the county where the land lies.

The county's Recording Forms page hosts the PTAX-203 with instructions and also lists the city deed forms. Land inside the city of Peoria adds paperwork of its own, summarized here from the county and city pages.

Peoria's city tax is $2.50 for each $1,000 of value, counting any fraction of $1,000, as stated on the declaration. The Clerk also computes each district's rate and posts levy, valuation and rate data by May 15 every year. A tax district search on the county site returns the districts for any address, and propertytax.peoriacounty.gov shows parcel details and bill history. Either office can say whether a prior year was sold before closing day.

What are the recent census numbers for Peoria County?

What is the address for recording a deed in Peoria County?

Is a transfer declaration required with a Peoria County deed?

How is the City of Peoria transfer tax set?

The city's instruction sheet prints $2.50 for each $1,000 of value or fraction of $1,000 stated on the declaration. Payment is made at the county recording office. Commercial or multi-family transfers need a zoning certificate from City Hall as well.

Will Peoria County raise recording fees?

The county posted a notice of a fee increase on January 1, 2027. The Clerk's Land Records page carries the current schedule, and the Clerk can quote a price for your document before you submit it.

Who accepts payment to redeem sold taxes in Peoria County?

The County Clerk. Pay once, in full, with cash, a cashier's check or a money order made out to the Peoria County Clerk. Payment plans and partial payments are not allowed, and an online estimate shows the next penalty date.

Sangamon County by the numbers

What does the Sangamon County Recorder of Deeds do?

The Sangamon County Recorder is the official land records office for the county, and it permanently records deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and liens. Its records go back to the early 1800s. Illinois counties call this office the Recorder, and in Sangamon County it is a grantor and grantee office, meaning every record is found by the name of the seller or the buyer.

The office also stores subdivision plats, land surveys, veteran discharge papers and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Its job is to keep an accurate chain of title, which is the series of recorded documents that title companies review before a closing. The office is on the first floor of the County Building at 200 South Ninth Street in Springfield, and the main number is (217) 535-3150.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Sangamon County?

A standard deed costs $64 to record, and a non-standard document that carries the Rental Housing Support surcharge costs $84. The county's fee schedule notes that a state law, HB3878, added $9.00 to the Rental Housing Support Fee in every Illinois county starting July 1, 2023.

Judgments, powers of attorney, notices of probate and death certificates are among the items the schedule lists as exceptions to the surcharge. Accepted payment is cash, check or credit card. Checks are made payable to the Sangamon County Recorder.

How is Illinois transfer tax charged on a Sangamon County sale?

The recorder's fee schedule prints the transfer tax stamp rate as $0.50 per $500 of value for the state plus $0.25 per $500 of value for the county. A sale of $100 or more requires a PTAX-203, the real estate transfer declaration, to accompany the deed so the tax can be set from the sale price.

  • A gift is exempt from transfer tax, but the deed must contain the matching exemption paragraph.
  • Other transfers can qualify for exemption, and the recorder posts an exemption list.
  • Most deeds of record carry revenue stamps that show the sale price, which is how people look up what a home sold for.

Rely on the closing agent to calculate the exact stamp amount for your price, since it follows the printed rates above.

What must a Sangamon County deed include before it is recorded?

The deed needs to be prepared, signed and notarized, and it must carry the details the recorder requires for indexing. The office says document preparation can need legal knowledge, and its staff cannot fill out forms or give legal advice. It recommends consulting an attorney.

  • The name and address of the preparer.
  • A return-to name and address.
  • A Tax Bill To name and address, if applicable.
  • The tax ID number and common address, which come from the Supervisor of Assessments at (217) 753-6805.
  • Black ink, on standard 8.5 by 11 paper with at least a 3 by 5 inch blank space in the upper right corner.

Documents are checked for statutory requirements and the fees are collected. They are recorded in the order received, given a document number, date and time, then scanned, indexed and verified.

How do I send a deed to the Sangamon County Recorder?

You can bring it to the first-floor office, mail the original with a check for the exact fee, or have a title company use eRecording. Mail goes to the Sangamon County Recorder, 200 South 9th Street, First Floor, Springfield, IL 62701, with the return address included.

The office states a goal of returning mailed originals in three to five business days, and another page of its FAQ says recorded documents come back within seven to ten business days. Plan for the longer figure if a lender is waiting on the paperwork. eRecording, handled by approved vendors, is meant to cut that to minutes and is mostly used by title companies, banks and law firms.

The online land records go back to 1982, deed books have been scanned to February 16, 1901, and older documents sit on microfiche in the office. Public terminals in the office are free.

What happens to the tax bill after a deed is recorded?

The recorder sends the deed electronically to the Supervisor of Assessments, who updates the ownership record, usually within 4 to 6 weeks. The deed also tells that office where to mail future tax bills.

An owner has to tell the Supervisor of Assessments about a new mailing address in writing, by fax or in person, because telephone requests are not accepted. A name change needs supporting paperwork such as a court order or marriage license, and removing a name after a death needs a death certificate and a recorded document.

Can the recorder run a title search or remove a lien?

No, the recorder cannot perform title searches or give legal advice about liens. By law the office can only show you the records it holds, and the staff recommend a title company for a full search and guarantee.

  • Lien records are checked in person at the recorder's office, not by phone.
  • A State tax lien question goes to the Illinois Department of Revenue State Tax Lien Unit at 217-785-5299.
  • For a federal tax lien, call 1-800-913-6050 for small business or self-employment liens and 1-800-829-7640 for wage or income liens.
  • An erroneous lien is a question for an attorney.

Lien releases are recorded with the office as well, and a seller who has paid off a lien should make sure the release is on record before closing.

What should a seller know about Sangamon County itself?

Sangamon County lies near the center of Illinois, is built around Springfield, the state capital and county seat, and was formed in 1821. The Census Bureau estimated 194,170 residents in July 2025 and 93,820 housing units, with 71.3% of occupied homes owner-occupied.

The median owner-occupied home value is $176,300, median gross rent is $983, and median household income is $75,357 for 2020 to 2024. Mean commute time is 19.7 minutes. Interstates 55 and 72 cross the county, and villages such as Chatham, Rochester, Riverton and Williamsville sit around Springfield.

Call the recorder before a closing if you are unsure whether a lien or release is on record.

More questions about Sangamon County, IL Recorder of Deeds

Where do I find the Sangamon County Recorder?

It is on the first floor of the County Building, 200 South Ninth Street, Springfield, IL 62701. The main phone number is (217) 535-3150, and press 2 for document requirements. Mailed documents go to the same address.

How much is the Sangamon County deed recording fee?

A standard deed costs $64, and a non-standard document with the Rental Housing Support surcharge costs $84. Exempt documents cost $45 for standard and $65 for non-standard. Make checks payable to the Sangamon County Recorder.

Do I need a PTAX-203 to record a deed in Sangamon County?

Yes, if the transfer is a sale of $100 or more, a PTAX-203 must accompany the deed. A gift is exempt from transfer tax, but the deed must carry the exemption paragraph. The posted exemption list covers other qualifying transfers.

How long does Sangamon County take to return a recorded deed?

The office aims for three to five business days on mailed originals. Its FAQ also says documents are returned within seven to ten business days. eRecording through a title company can finish in minutes.

Are Sangamon County land records online?

Yes, data and images from 1982 forward are online, and deed books are scanned back to February 16, 1901. Some search options carry a charge, such as the Tapestry service, while a data-only search is free. Public terminals in the office are free to use.

St Clair County by the numbers

Where do St. Clair County deeds go to be recorded?

Belleville is home to the St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds, and every deed for land inside the county lands there. State law (765 ILCS 5/28) ties recording to the county of the land, so a Belleville house is never recorded in Madison or Monroe County, whatever the seller's address.

Why bother? Under 765 ILCS 5/30, a deed binds later buyers and creditors only from the time it is filed. A signed deed sitting in a drawer protects nobody.

The counter is staffed on weekdays starting at 8:30 AM and closing at 5:00 PM. Seven public workstations let anyone search the land records without charge, and a printout from those machines costs $2.00 per page.

What does recording cost at the St. Clair County Recorder?

The recorder prints a two-column price list. One column includes the RHSP surcharge and one leaves it out. Deeds, leases and easements carry transfer tax on top when it applies, and the office takes cash, or a check or money order written to Recorder of Deeds.

Any document notarized before August 1, 2005 is also exempt. Unsure which row fits? The office asks you to call first.

How do I mail a deed to the St. Clair County Recorder?

Two addresses exist, and the carrier decides which. Regular mail goes to Recorder of Deeds, PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222. FedEx and UPS packages go to Recorder of Deeds, #10 Public Sq, 5th Floor, Belleville, IL 62220.

A complete package holds four things:

  • The original signed and notarized deed.
  • The Illinois transfer declaration.
  • Payment for the fee in the matching row, plus any transfer tax.
  • A return address for the recorded copy.

In a typical sale, the escrow officer or lawyer at the closing sends in the deed and pays the fees.

How does the Illinois transfer tax work on a St. Clair County sale?

The state tax is fifty cents for each $500 slice of stated value, with a leftover remainder counted as one more slice (35 ILCS 200/31-10), and a mortgage that stays in place is subtracted from the figure. The recorder collects it and reports through the state's MyDec system. Because the St. Clair schedule says transfer tax is added to deeds "when applicable," confirm the amount with the office before you mail payment.

A deed can be exempt. Section 31-45 lists a few kinds that sellers meet in practice:

  • A deed given for actual consideration under $100.
  • A deed that fixes or confirms an earlier recorded one with no new consideration.
  • A tax deed or a deed of partition.
  • A deed to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of it.
  • A deed to or from a governmental body.

Some exempt deeds still have to be filed with a declaration, such as deeds to or from a governmental body or a property exchange.

What goes on the transfer declaration for a St. Clair County deed?

The declaration is the form that rides with the deed. It is due at presentation, or within 3 business days after the transfer if that comes first, and at least one seller and one buyer sign (35 ILCS 200/31-25). Their attorneys or agents may sign for them.

It asks for the value, parcel number, legal description, deed date, property address, type of improvement, lot size, related-party status and homestead exemptions on the last tax bill. A deed submitted without a complete declaration can be refused.

The parcel number also unlocks the county's online index, which wants it typed as 00-00-0-000-000.

How can I search and copy St. Clair County land records?

Fidlar Technologies runs the county's remote access, and there are three tiers. AVA Search is free but returns data only, by party name, recorded date range, parcel number, document number or document type, and shows no images.

Tapestry Eon charges $8.75 per index or image search, with image viewing included, plus $1.00 for each printed page. Heavy users can open a Laredo Anywhere account on one of five minute plans: $75.00 a month for 0 to 250 minutes, $125.00 for 251 to 500, $200.00 for 501 to 1000, $300.00 for 1001 to 2000, or $400.00 for unlimited minutes. Overage runs from $.25 down to $.15 per minute, and Laredo prints cost $.35 per page. Laredo sign-ups go through recorder@co.st-clair.il.us.

For paper copies from the office:

  • Every request needs a document number or a book and page number.
  • Under 10 non-certified copies can be requested by phone at 618-825-2481 or 618-825-2482, or by email.
  • Certified copies and requests for 10 or more go by mail with a check for the full amount.
  • Standard 8.5 by 11 copies cost $2.00 a page. Full plats cost $5.00 a page, and 30 by 36 plats cost $10.00 on page one and $5.00 on every added page.
  • UCC and state or federal tax lien copies are $1.00 a page.
  • A certified copy is priced at the original recording fee, less the $10 surcharge where it applies.

Certified copies of a DD-214 are free, but only the veteran, dependents, the county veterans' service officer and other authorized people may obtain a full copy.

What does a St. Clair County seller need to know about the area?

St. Clair County stretches across 674 square miles east of St. Louis, in the Metro East part of Southern Illinois. It was created in 1790, and the 2020 count was 257,400 people. The 2025 estimate is 250,708. Urban areas hold 85.8 percent of the population, and the central part of the county sits on a bluff above the Mississippi River where suburban housing keeps spreading around Belleville.

The 2020 census listed 114,595 housing units, with 65.1 percent of occupied ones owned and 34.9 percent rented. Cities include Belleville, O'Fallon, Fairview Heights, Collinsville (partly), East St. Louis, Cahokia Heights, Mascoutah, Lebanon, Madison and Columbia (partly). The eastern and southern parts are thinly settled farmland.

Buyers weigh commute and school district. Interstates 55, 64, 70 and 255 cross the county, and 11 MetroLink stations sit on the Red and Blue Lines. Scott Air Force Base is inside the county. Elementary districts include Belleville 118, O'Fallon 90 and Belle Valley 11, while high school districts include Belleville Township 201, O'Fallon Township 203 and Freeburg 77.

A Belleville-area home that needs work can still sell as is for cash, and the closing agent files with the recorder.

Who records deeds in St. Clair County, Illinois?

The Recorder of Deeds in Belleville. Mail documents to PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222, or to the 5th Floor of #10 Public Sq for overnight carriers.

What does the Recorder charge for a deed?

The printed schedule shows $55.00 with the RHSP surcharge and $36.00 without it. Transfer tax is added when it applies, so get the final figure from the recorder's staff.

Do I need a transfer declaration with a St. Clair County deed?

Yes. It is signed by a seller and a buyer and filed with the deed or within 3 business days of the transfer. Some exempt deeds still need one.

Is any St. Clair County record search free?

Yes, for index data. AVA Search lists names, dates, parcel numbers and document types without images. Images need Tapestry Eon or a Laredo Anywhere account.

What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?

The statute taxes each $500 of value, or fraction of it, at fifty cents. Foreclosure deeds to a mortgage holder and deeds under $100 in consideration are exempt.

Where does a Winnebago County deed get recorded?

The Winnebago County Recorder's Office, Room 405 in the County Administration Building at 404 Elm Street, Rockford, IL 61101, files every deed for property in the county. Call (815) 319-4325. Service hours are weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

Land records for the whole county live here, and the books run from hand-written volumes of the 1830s to the electronic index the office uses now. Held in the office: deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and surveys, Uniform Commercial Code filings, corporation documents and military discharges. The county was organized in 1836, and one office serves Rockford, Loves Park, South Beloit and every township around them. With 285,350 residents and 115,459 households at the 2020 census, it handles the paperwork for the seventh most populous county in Illinois.

The staff index and preserve what is handed in. Drafting is outside their role: they cannot help prepare a document or pick a deed type, and the most they will do is point out missing information when a document is presented. Plan on a lawyer or closing agent to draft the deed.

What are the Winnebago County recording fees?

A document that meets the standard format is recorded for $54.00. That figure comes from a predictable fee schedule the county board adopted on December 12, 2024 to match Public Act 103-0884, and the schedule started January 1, 2025. Payment can be cash, check or card, with no bill over $50 accepted.

The $12.00 extra applies when a document breaks the format rules or cites six or more parcel numbers or six or more document numbers. For plats, one full copy is all the office needs from January 2025, and a missing copy adds $4.00 per page. Photocopies cannot be recorded, and each submission must show a name and address for return.

What format keeps a deed at the standard Winnebago County fee?

The county's forms page repeats the state standard from 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.2. In plain terms:

  • Loose sheets of 8.5 by 11 inches, not bound for good and not a continuous form; attached graphics can run to 11 by 17.
  • Black ink throughout, by hand, typewriter or printer. Colored signatures and dates are fine if they copy clearly.
  • White stock rated 20 pounds or heavier, with half an inch of clear margin on the top, bottom and both sides.
  • The top right of page one left empty, in a space of 3 by 5 inches.
  • No staples or attachments fixed to any page.

Blank samples on the county site cover a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, a joint tenancy warranty deed, a tenancy by the entirety warranty deed and a Plat Act affidavit. The page warns that the office provides no help filling them out.

What do MyDec and the Illinois transfer tax mean for a sale?

Winnebago County has required an online transfer declaration from the state's MyDec portal since July 1, 2023, for any conveyance priced at $100 or more. Its status has to read "Closing Completed" when the deed is presented, and a paper PTAX-203 is refused. Anyone with internet access can prepare it in advance.

Separately, the state taxes the transfer itself, in Article 31 of the Property Tax Code (35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70), and the county recorder collects the money. Section 31-15 prints the stamp rate as 50¢ per $500 of value or fraction of $500. Paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, with electronic stamps or other indicia after that. The final amount on a given sale follows the declaration, so your closing agent can quote it.

How can you search Winnebago County land records?

Phone searches are not offered. Visitors can ask at the front desk, or use the public stations when more than five searches are needed, and printed copies cost $0.50 per page.

  • Direct Search: free, limited, basic details only, with no images of documents.
  • Tapestry: pay as you go. The office lists $6.95 per search, with an increase to $8.75 effective September 1, 2023, and $1.00 per printed page.
  • Laredo: set up for commercial users, and both Laredo and Tapestry sell subscriptions.
  • Mail and email requests: $10.00 per search for documents under 20 years old, $29.00 for older ones, and $10.00 plus $4.00 per page for plats. The cap is five searches per request, and email answers can take two business days.

For maps, WinGIS is the county's geographic information site, and the number for subscriptions is (815) 319-4450. A state database of Department of Revenue tax liens is also searchable online, which suits a pre-listing lien check.

What is the Property Fraud Alert in Winnebago County?

Anyone can enroll at no cost. Give your name, pick phone, email or text, and you are notified each time a recorded document matches. It cannot block a filing, but it lets you react quickly if something is wrong, and a Spanish version exists.

State law now adds a second layer. Public Act 104-0382, in force January 1, 2026, makes each county set up a fraud referral and review process for recorded instruments. A June 1, 2026 notice from the Recorder said the process would begin on or after September 8, 2026, and that a deed which looks forged, altered or aimed at clouding title may be sent to administrative review.

The office also flags mailers that offer to sell owners a copy of their deed. They do not come from any government office, and the same record can be had from the Recorder at the posted copy fees.

What deed and mortgage paperwork does a Winnebago County seller need?

Lenders do not hold the deed. The office calls that a common misconception: the deed came back to the owner shortly after purchase, and the paper that shows a loan is satisfied is the Release of Mortgage, recorded in this same office. If you paid off a loan long ago and have no release, search the records now so a buyer's file is complete.

When the owner has died, the office urges legal advice, noting that a new deed has to be prepared and recorded and that it cannot name the deed type. Typical order of work:

  • Draft the deed to the format rules above.
  • Finish the MyDec declaration until it shows "Closing Completed."
  • Present the original, with a return address and the fee.
  • File the recorded copy, plus any old mortgage release, with the closing papers.

More questions about Winnebago County, IL Recorder of Deeds

What is the Winnebago County fee for a standard deed?

$54.00. A deed that breaks the format rules or names six or more parcel numbers is $66.00, and veteran discharge papers record free.

Is the paper PTAX-203 still accepted in Winnebago County?

No. Since July 1, 2023 conveyances of $100 or more need a MyDec declaration that reads Closing Completed.

Will the Winnebago County Recorder draft a deed for me?

No. Drafting and choosing a deed type are outside the office's role, and staff only note missing information at presentation.

Where can I get a recorded Winnebago County deed copy?

At the counter, through the online search sites, or by mail or email request. Plain copies are $0.50 per page; certified copies are $35.00 per document.

Can I be warned when something is recorded against my property?

Yes. Enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert and a matching recording triggers a phone, email or text notice.
